Hi Rachel —

I signed up via your quickstart and kicked the tires on the GitHub connector. We're an open-source maintainer org (OpenRepo) and have a couple of questions before booking a deeper demo:

- Can the integration work as a GitHub App installed to a single repo instead of org-wide? We want to minimize permissions.
- What minimal scopes do you need for repo-level installs (read-only vs write for webhooks/PR comments)?
- How long do webhook payloads live on your side? We have strict retention needs for security audits.

Happy to jump on a 30-min demo next week — I'm PST (San Francisco). We filled in the calendar fields on signup but didn't see webhook examples there. Attaching a short excerpt of the webhook payload we collect (example-webhook-log.txt).

Hi Samir —

3:00 PM PST on Wed 12/9 is perfect — updated invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=updated-invite

Quick answers ahead of the call so we can use the meeting for the demo and any deeper security details:
- Repo vs org install: Most integrations can be configured per-repo. Only a few features (org-wide analytics and automated repo discovery) require org-level install; we'll show those and how to scope them down.
- Minimal scopes: read-only for Issues/PRs + webhooks is common; write scopes are optional and can be limited. Marissa will demo where write access is used and how to restrict it.
- Webhook retention: Redwood stores recent webhook payloads for 14 days by default for replay/debug but we can turn off retention or extend per-contract for enterprise. Monica will share the security questionnaire and policy during the call.

Agenda:
- 3:00–3:05 PM: quick intros
- 3:05–3:20 PM: live install demo (repo-level install) + webhook mapping
- 3:20–3:30 PM: retention/security Q&A and next steps (SLA/contract intro if useful)

Attachments: security-questionnaire.pdf (sent earlier)

See you Wednesday —
Aditya
